authoredBy: Riki Taylor (creative decisions), executed deterministically by the AAMP flagship pipeline

painPoints: The cards they care about sit across different promotions, broadcasters and time zones
The schedule lives in a group chat nobody maintains, so they find out after the fact
Having an opinion about a fight and having nowhere to put it before the result lands
strategy.positioning: The one place the whole of combat sports is already organised: what is on, who is fighting, what the room thinks, and where you rank once it is over.
strategy.targetAudienceSummary: Combat sports fans aged 18-34 who follow more than one promotion and argue about results after every card
keyMessages: Every card that matters, in one place
Predict before the first bell, then see where you rank
The discussion is part of the product, not an afterthought
toneGuidelines: Certain, never shouty — the product does the talking
Red is a signal, not a wash

creativeDirection.logline: The missed start becomes the reason to open it, and the product answers in four escalating moves.
creativeDirection.visualDirection: Black base, crushed shadows, one saturated red. Footage graded into a single palette so eight separately-shot plates read as one film; product screens left ungraded because legibility outranks palette unity. Movement is always toward the product: a slow push on the hook, a controlled ramp through the sport, then bezelled phone compositions that hold still long enough to be read. Type is one uppercase display voice, bottom-anchored inside the safe area, never crossing an interface. Glow is reserved for the accent, and the accent is reserved for the two moments that matter — the prediction and the call to action.
creativeDirection.narrativeArc: Tension first: you missed it again. Then breadth, so the fix is not one promotion. Then the real events screen, which is the first honest proof. Then a landed strike, which is the reason anyone cared in the first place, resolving straight into the real prediction interface. Then the leaderboard, which turns a private opinion into a public position. Then the discussion, which is where the argument goes. Then the mark, and one true instruction.
referenceNotes: Pacing accelerates through the middle and decelerates hard into the CTA hold
Each product beat holds long enough that a viewer could actually read one line
Every transition is motivated: impact, match or interface reveal, never a template wipe

hook.strategy: Open on the tension rather than the product. A near-black frame with one red source and a line that names the failure the audience already has.

beats.description: Near-black plate, red light drifting behind rain. Slow push in. The line lands almost immediately and names the failure before anything is sold.
A black glove over a deep red-lit floor, opening quick and settling. The sport itself, in the brand's own two colours, under the app's own words.
The real events screen, bezelled on a blurred backplate and held still for two seconds so the heading and the upcoming card can actually be read. The first honest proof in the cut.
Real contact in a dark gym, entering on a whip and landing on a flash. The reason anyone has an opinion, placed immediately before the interface that takes it.
The real fight card, framed on the bout and the community split. A tap indicator marks the prediction bar. Everything on this screen is the product's own data, not typeset copy.
The real leaderboard, with its own explanation of the challenge visible and its identities already redacted. This is the social payoff: a private opinion becomes a public position.
A declared PRODUCT_MOCKUP of the card-talk discussion interface, bezelled and held. Geometry in the brand's colours with the real mark: no handles, no comments, no counts, no text of any kind.
Dip to black onto the designed end card carrying the real mark, then the headline and the one true instruction, held still to the last frame.

cta.headline: NEVER MISS FIGHT NIGHT.
cta.subline: OPEN COMBAT REVIEWS · Every combat sport. One place.

factualConstraints: PRODUCT — Coverage: Combat Reviews lists events across multiple combat-sports promotions in one app.
PRODUCT — Events screen: the events screen shows upcoming fights with predictions, full cards, venues, broadcasters and live countdowns.
PRODUCT — Fight card: an event's fight card shows bout order, round counts and estimated start times, with the community prediction split shown per bout.
PRODUCT — Predictions: points are earned from correct predictions in the CombatReviews Challenge, ranked on a leaderboard by prediction accuracy.
PRODUCT — Not betting: the CombatReviews Challenge is skill, not betting. Combat Reviews is not a betting product and takes no stakes.
PRODUCT — Discussion: each event carries a card-talk discussion region where fans talk about the card.
PRODUCT — How it is opened: Combat Reviews is reached on the web; there is no verified public store listing, so no store badge and no download promise may appear.
PROHIBITION — no authored copy names a fighter, an event, a date, a vote total, a percentage split or a countdown.
PROHIBITION — the storyboard is REFERENCE_ONLY; no frame of it may appear.
PROHIBITION — no agency, studio or existing campaign may be named or imitated.
